_about: Style configurations: one entry per current (movement or school). Schema and rules: docs/styles/README.md. Detail and sources: each entry's doc. Merged from the research batches in studio/styles.parts/ (2026-11-25).

byzantine-icon.name: Byzantine and Orthodox icon painting
byzantine-icon.period: Byzantium and the Orthodox world, 6th-15th c. and continuing (post-Byzantine, Russian)
technique: roskrysh: flat dark local colour first

palette.principle: few mineral and earth pigments in flat symbolic zones, modelled dark to light; gold as the field of light

byzantine-icon.light: no source in the scene and no cast shadows; light is the gold ground and the final highlights and ozhivki
byzantine-icon.value_key: middle-dark figures on a high-key gold field (judgement)
byzantine-icon.composition: central, frontal, near-symmetric figure filling the panel against gold; inscriptions; inverse perspective in scenes
byzantine-icon.drawing: contour first, incised or painted lines restored at the end; conventional types and proportions
byzantine-icon.edges: crisp drawn outlines; smooth transitions only inside faces through floats

marks.direction: hatched along form; highlight lines follow folds and features

process: prepare panel: recess, linen, many gesso layers, polish
draw and incise the design
bole and gold leaf on ground and haloes, burnish
repaint guide lines
roskrysh: flat dark local colour; sankir on flesh and hair
highlights in progressively lighter, smaller layers, each floated with a transparent glaze
last sparing highlights; golden glaze unifies the face
restore final lines
ozhivki and gold assist lines
inscriptions
finishing: olifa (linseed oil with resin) over the cured tempera for a warm amber depth; no faked age or soot
pitfalls: pastiche: gold background plus sad face without the layered build; fake cracks or soot
melodrama or expressive gesture
sentimental devotional-print sweetness
a Renaissance perspective box with gold behind it
Teodor's hushed bittersweet interior habit
careless imitation of liturgical inscriptions
engine_gaps: no gilding (gold leaf on bole, burnished, reflective)
egg tempera medium not yet available (fast drying, hatching, no wet blending)
no olifa finishing op
scene blockouts render linear perspective only; inverse perspective needs a hand-drawn SVG schema
no incising tool; no lettering tool for inscriptions
judgement_calls: all hex values approximate the named pigments
sources: Met Heilbrunn Timeline, Icons and Iconoclasm in Byzantium: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/icons-and-iconoclasm-in-byzantium
Museum of Russian Icons, Creation of an Icon: https://www.iconmuseum.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/Creation-of-an-Icon.pdf

Met Heilbrunn Timeline, Painting in Oil in the Low Countries and Its Spread to Southern Europe (tempera handling): https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/painting-in-oil-in-the-low-countries-and-its-spread-to-southern-europe

layer_order.source: docs/styles/byzantine-icon.md section 9: design drawn and incised; roskrysh (flat dark local colour); highlights in progressively lighter layers, each floated with a transparent glaze; last sparing highlights; final lines restored.
layer_order.judgement: roskrysh mapped to dead_colour; the hatched highlight layers and the floats share one stage because they alternate.

renaissance.name: Renaissance painting (Early and High, Italy and the North)
renaissance.period: Italy and the Low Countries, c. 1420-1520
technique: sfumato (blending by thinning the top layer)

palette.principle: clear local colours modelled in value within each zone; ultramarine and red lake as climaxes; earths and greens for landscape

renaissance.light: one steady daylight source from the side; soft, transparent-looking shadows in oil
renaissance.value_key: middle, full range in oil; lighter and more even in tempera
renaissance.composition: single-point linear perspective, vanishing point on the horizon; centralised or pyramidal groups; architecture or measured landscape
renaissance.drawing: underdrawing first; form modelled in light; idealised proportion; firm early contours, sfumato in the High Renaissance
renaissance.edges: crisp in early tempera; lost, smoky edges in High Renaissance flesh, with structure kept

marks.direction: follows form; hatching in tempera

process: panel with gesso and glue ground
underdrawing in a fluid dark medium
light grey oil priming
monochrome underpainting in dark yellow, brown, blackish-brown
colour lay-in per zone (e.g. grey, azurite, then ultramarine for blue drapery)
flesh in opaque layers, shadows blended by thinning the top layer
glazes and scumbles for rich drapery
final details and small gilded accents
finishing: final unifying glazes
small mordant-gilded accents if any
varnish (judgement: standard practice)
pitfalls: pastiche: enigmatic smile, overall blur, perspective grid as decoration, fake craquelure
sentimental pseudo-Renaissance sweetness
cold diagrammatic geometry
Baroque darkness creeping in via dark grounds
engine_gaps: egg tempera medium (hatching, fast drying) not yet available
no gilding
no varnish finishing op
glaze is a uniform regional mix, not a brushed transparent layer
no per-pigment K and S (glaze transparency vs opacity)
unverified: green-earth flesh underlayer, three-value tempera modelling and varnish in Cennini: located, not read this session
sources: Met Heilbrunn Timeline, Painting in Oil in the Low Countries and Its Spread to Southern Europe: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/painting-in-oil-in-the-low-countries-and-its-spread-to-southern-europe
Warburg Institute, Following Alberti's advice: the fifteenth-century shift to oil paint: https://omeka.warburg.sas.ac.uk/exhibits/show/paintinggoldthread-slug/3bellini-slug
Keith, Roy, Morrison, Schade 2011, National Gallery Technical Bulletin 32 (Virgin of the Rocks): https://www.nationalgallery.org.uk/upload/pdf/keith_roy_morrison_schade2011.pdf
Shafe, Cennini's Il Libro dell'Arte, the panel painter's workshop: https://www.shafe.co.uk/essay_panel_painters_workshop/
C. Cennini, Il Libro dell'Arte, trans. D. V. Thompson 1933 (located, not read): https://ia801802.us.archive.org/20/items/illibrodellarte1933cenn/illibrodellarte1933cenn.pdf

layer_order.source: docs/styles/renaissance.md section 9: underdrawing; monochrome underpainting; lay-in of colour per zone; flesh in opaque layers; glazes and scumbles for drapery; final details.
layer_order.judgement: the colour lay-in per zone mapped to dead_colour.

baroque.name: Baroque chiaroscuro and tenebrism
baroque.period: Rome c. 1600, spreading across Europe to c. 1670 (Caravaggisti, Spain, Utrecht, Rembrandt)
technique: late dark accents and shadow glazes

palette.principle: limited earth palette on a brown ground; few saturated accents; colour lives only in the light

baroque.light: one strong focused source, high and to one side, no reflected light; shadows merge into the dark ground
baroque.value_key: low, with a narrow band of high lights
baroque.composition: half- or three-quarter figures close to the picture plane; shallow dark stage; diagonals; tight cropping; a moment of action or recognition
baroque.drawing: from live models, unidealised; incised lines and broad abbozzo instead of full drawing; form carved by light
baroque.edges: hard where light meets dark; lost where shadow meets background

marks.direction: follows form in lights; broad in darks

process: warm or dark coloured ground
pose model and light; incise key contours
abbozzo: broad brush indications of forms
build the lights thickly in lead-white-rich paint; let dry
final paint in one or two layers, ground kept as mid-tone
late brown ground-coloured paint to sharpen darks
shadow glazes feathered onto lights
finishing: strongest highlights and dark accents last
varnish (judgement)
do not exaggerate ground darkness for an aged look
pitfalls: pastiche: black background plus spotlight; candle kitsch; brown sauce; faked craquelure
horror-film menace or cheap theatricality; gloom without an event
Teodor's lit doorway in a dark warm room habit
muddy value collapse without a narrow high band
engine_gaps: no incising tool
exposed ground has no transparency, it is only unpainted ground colour
no varnish finishing op
judgement_calls: most of the pigment list (standard practice)
sources: Met Heilbrunn Timeline, Caravaggio and His Followers: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/caravaggio-michelangelo-merisi-1571-1610-and-his-followers
L. Keith 1998, Three Paintings by Caravaggio, National Gallery Technical Bulletin 19: https://www.nationalgallery.org.uk/research/research-resources/technical-bulletin/three-paintings-by-caravaggio
P. Noble 2025, The Role of the Colored Ground in Rembrandt's Painting Practice, JHNA 17:2: https://jhna.org/articles/the-role-of-the-colored-ground-in-rembrandts-painting-practice/
E. Kolfin 2025, Why Colored Grounds Matter, JHNA 17:2: https://jhna.org/articles/why-colored-grounds-matter-evolving-research-colored-grounds-in-dutch-paintings-1580-1720/

layer_order.source: docs/styles/baroque.md section 9: incised contours; abbozzo (broad brushstrokes indicating forms); lights built thickly, final paint in one or two layers; late ground-coloured darks; shadow glazes feathered onto the lights.
layer_order.judgement: the abbozzo mapped to underpainting; the late darks (accents) and the shadow glazes share the last stage.

dutch-golden-age.name: Dutch Golden Age painting (genre scenes, still life, landscape)
technique: thin semi-transparent shadows over the ground

palette.principle: restrained, harmonised earths with a few precious accents; near-monochrome tonal palette for banquet pieces and tonal landscapes; fuller colour after 1650
avoid: cool greys unrelated to the ground

dutch-golden-age.light: side window daylight in interiors; candle or hearth night pieces; diffuse daylight under a large sky in landscape
dutch-golden-age.composition: measured interior box with figures in quiet occupation; tabletop still life seen slightly from above with an overhanging edge; low horizon and large sky in landscape
dutch-golden-age.drawing: observational and accurate; form built tonally over the dead colour; textures through value and highlight
dutch-golden-age.edges: soft where ground shows between light and shadow; crisp on highlights and detail

marks.direction: follows form; smooth

process: warm coloured ground (chalk-glue plus oil priming on panel; grey over red on canvas)
sketch the composition on the ground
dead colouring: monochrome brown underpainting of composition and light
working up each area in one or two sessions, back to front: lights in body colour, shadows thin over the ground
glazes to deepen and unify
impasto highlights and last accents, ground left between light and shadow
finishing: unifying glazes
small impasto highlights
varnish (judgement)
pitfalls: pastiche: pearl earring, maid at a window, skull and candle, fake yellow varnish
sterile photographic hyperrealism
decorative Victorian clutter
Baroque spotlight drama
Teodor's hushed doorway habit
tonal treated as grey instead of warm harmonised earths
engine_gaps: glaze is a uniform regional mix, not brushed transparent paint
no per-pigment transparency
no varnish finishing op
fijnschilder detail beyond canvas resolution
judgement_calls: pigment list and hex values (standard practice)
sources: Met Heilbrunn Timeline, Genre Painting in Northern Europe: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/genre-painting-in-northern-europe
Met Heilbrunn Timeline, Still-Life Painting in Northern Europe, 1600-1800: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/still-life-painting-in-northern-europe-1600-1800
Met Heilbrunn Timeline, Landscape Painting in the Netherlands: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/landscape-painting-in-the-netherlands
E. Kolfin 2025, Why Colored Grounds Matter, JHNA 17:2: https://jhna.org/articles/why-colored-grounds-matter-evolving-research-colored-grounds-in-dutch-paintings-1580-1720/
Essential Vermeer, Working up (after van de Wetering): https://www.essentialvermeer.com/technique/technique_working_up.html
P. Noble 2025, The Role of the Colored Ground in Rembrandt's Painting Practice, JHNA 17:2: https://jhna.org/articles/the-role-of-the-colored-ground-in-rembrandts-painting-practice/

layer_order.source: docs/styles/dutch-golden-age.md section 9: sketch on the ground; dead colouring (a monochrome brown underpainting); working up area by area; glazes to deepen and unify; impasto highlights and last accents.
layer_order.judgement: the Dutch dead colouring is monochrome, so underpainting and dead_colour are one stage.

romanticism.name: Romanticism (the sublime landscape and the British watercolour tradition)

palette.principle: atmosphere over local colour; warm-cool polarity of light against storm; few pigments with tonal gradation; in watercolour the paper is the light

romanticism.light: the protagonist: breaking through cloud, low sun, moon, fire or storm; a bright centre in a turbulent surround, or a graded sky over dark land
romanticism.value_key: wide range; varies from high-key atmospheric to low-key nocturne
romanticism.composition: low horizon and big sky; edge-to-edge emptiness without framing foreground; storm vortex around a light centre; tiny figures against vast nature
romanticism.drawing: two poles: form dissolved into atmosphere, or precise drawing veiled by thin paint
romanticism.edges: lost in sky and distance; a few crisp edges near the focus; in watercolour soft wet edges early, hard dry edges later

marks.length: long in skies, short for detail
marks.direction: sweeps with the weather; stipple for mist

process: decide horizon and light; underdrawing (ruled for architecture, freer for nature)
colour beginning: thin warm then cool washes (watercolour) or thin transparent tonal washes (oil)
sky and distance wet-in-wet or scumbled; veil forms with sky paint
middle and near forms in harder-edged strokes
lights: lifted, rubbed, scratched or reserved (watercolour); selective impasto (oil)
last telling details and small figures
finishing: oil: varnish (judgement)
watercolour: no varnish; stop when telling details are placed and lights lifted
restraint: leave the atmosphere open
pitfalls: pastiche: wanderer above a sea of fog; generic orange sunset vortex; calendar mountains
Teodor's lone figure from behind habit (the Rückenfigur): avoid unless commissioned
kitsch fantasy-cover grandeur
soft-focus nostalgia; gloom without awe; picturesque prettiness without threat
overworked muddy watercolour
engine_gaps: watercolour and gouache media not yet in v8 (blooms, granulation, staining, hard drying edges, body colour)
no lifting, sponging, scratching-out or reserve/masking tools
no gum arabic gloss
no toned-paper support
glaze is a regional mix, not a broken scumble
no varnish finishing op
judgement_calls: most hex values and the period-pigment list beyond Friedrich's
felt_bias (the painter's feeling picks the stormy or still pole)
sources: Llewellyn and Riding (eds) 2013, The Art of the Sublime, Tate: https://www.tate.org.uk/art/research-publications/the-sublime/the-romantic-sublime-r1109221
Met Heilbrunn Timeline, Watercolor Painting in Britain, 1750-1850: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/watercolor-painting-in-britain-1750-1850
Smarthistory, Caspar David Friedrich, Monk by the Sea: https://smarthistory.org/friedrich-monk-by-the-sea
National Gallery, Winter Landscape close examination: https://www.nationalgallery.org.uk/research/research-resources/research-papers/close-examination/winter-landscape
Wallace Collection, Turner's watercolour materials and techniques: https://www.wallacecollection.org/explore/explore-in-depth/turner/turners-watercolors/turners-watercolour-materials-and-techniques/

layer_order.source: docs/styles/romanticism.md section 9: underdrawing; thin transparent tonal washes (oil) or warm then cool washes (watercolour); sky and distance scumbled or wet-in-wet; middle and near forms in harder strokes; last telling details.
layer_order.judgement: lifted, scratched or rubbed lights are corrections and not ordered.

cubism.name: Cubism (Analytic and Synthetic)
technique: charcoal drawing then selective thin oil
Synthetic: flat planes, pattern and texture over them

palette.principle: Analytic: near-monochrome browns, greys, ochres and black (Met, Tate); Synthetic: simpler shapes, brighter flat colours (Tate). Hexes are judgement.
avoid: strong hue in Analytic mode beyond one accent

cubism.light: no single source; each facet carries its own small light-to-dark shift, light as rhythm across planes (judgement)
cubism.value_key: middle, narrow range in Analytic; contrast between whole shapes in Synthetic (judgement)
cubism.composition: upright or oval table-top still life seen from several viewpoints; dense interlocking centre thinning to bare ground at the edges; letters flat on the picture plane (Met, Tate)
cubism.drawing: objects dissected into small facets and reassembled; charcoal outlines on, under and beside the paint; open contours so planes slide together; recognisable clues anchor the subject (Met)
cubism.edges: facets hard on one side, lost into the neighbour on the other (judgement, 'passage'); Synthetic edges crisp

marks.direction: parallel within each facet, one angle per plane (judgement)

process: thin smooth white ground
charcoal drawing of the main elements
selective thin oil, washes, bare ground left
facet building with small parallel strokes, densest at centre
more charcoal on and beside the paint
darkest accents and stencilled letters last
finishing: check the centre is the densest area
last dark accents and lettering
no unifying glaze; surface left matte (judgement)
pitfalls: pastiche: guitar, bottle and 'JOURNAL'
random shattered-glass triangles over a realist picture
kaleidoscope colour in Analytic mode
machine-flat vector planes in Synthetic mode
nearest wrong feelings: cold detachment, chaos/anxiety
engine_gaps: one medium per canvas: no charcoal over oil
no stencil tool
no sand/texture additive
no pasted paper (by rule: paint its look)
needs a schema helper that recuts a blockout into planes from several viewpoints

layer_order.source: docs/styles/cubism.md section 9: charcoal drawing; selective thin oil and washes; facets of small parallel strokes; more charcoal on and beside the paint; darkest accents and letters last.
layer_order.judgement: the second charcoal campaign over the paint mapped to contour.

post-impressionism.name: Post-Impressionism

technique: parallel hatched strokes and colour patches

marks.direction: parallel hatching at one diagonal per passage (judgement)

technique: dots, dabs and dashes of minimally mixed prismatic colour, unblended

marks.direction: alternating size and direction at edges

technique: flat colour planes in dark outlines (cloisonnism)

marks.direction: follows form and rhythm; swirls only where the subject asks

palette.principle: colour as structure or feeling rather than record: modulated patches (constructive), minimally mixed prismatic dots (divisionist), boldly exaggerated complementaries (expressive)

post-impressionism.light: light from colour, not chiaroscuro; luminosity from high-chroma light pigments; symbolic light in the expressive mode
post-impressionism.composition: stable architectural (constructive), planned frieze with painted border (divisionist), high viewpoint and flattened print-like depth (expressive)
post-impressionism.drawing: form as planes with blue contour restated (constructive); contours enlarged around figures (divisionist); heavy dark outlines and deformation for mood (expressive)
post-impressionism.edges: built by adjacent planes; haloed by alternating dots; or hard dark contour lines around flat fields

marks.direction: per mode

process: constructive: pencil sketch, thin blue outline, hatched strokes from thin washes to rich layers over the whole, impasto rework of the focal area, stop with ground showing
divisionist: Impressionist-like first campaign, dry, second campaign of unblended prismatic dots with contours reinforced, painted border last
expressive: contour drawing, colour fields wet into wet, impasto in proportion to feeling, dark outlines restated last (judgement)
finishing: constructive: may stop unfinished, ground visible, edges incomplete; no unifying glaze
divisionist: painted inner border as the final stage; white frame
expressive: last outlines and accents; no varnish tone (judgement)
pitfalls: swirl and sunflower pastiche
pointillism as an even dot filter over a finished image
geometric faceting without colour modulation
complementaries mixed into mud
decorative cheerfulness or sterile system instead of feeling
Teodor's hushed bittersweet habit
engine_gaps: no native dot or hatch primitive (free with short length and narrow spread approximates)
no rule placing complementaries side by side
do_match blends divisionist dots away; dots must be free intentions
watercolour medium not built yet

layer_order.source: docs/styles/post-impressionism.md section 9 and styles.json process: pencil sketch and thin blue outline; hatched strokes from thin washes to rich layers (constructive) or a first campaign (divisionist) or colour fields (expressive); impasto rework of the focal area, dots, dark outlines restated last.
layer_order.judgement: one order for the three modes; the last stage holds the impasto accents and the restated contours.

surrealism.name: Surrealism (illusionistic and automatist)
surrealism.period: Paris and Europe, 1924 to the Second World War
technique: illusionistic: precise underdrawing, thin smooth modelling, hidden brushwork
automatist: automatic drawing, stained or scumbled field, chance textures (frottage, grattage, decalcomania) worked back into

palette.principle: illusionistic: naturalistic, controlled colour, strong colour only on the strange object; automatist: one field colour, black line, a few primaries (judgement; Magritte's smoky greys/blues/earths then lighter, MoMA)

surrealism.light: illusionistic: one low raking light, long sharp cast shadows, everything legible; automatist: little modelling (judgement)
surrealism.value_key: illusionistic: high-key sky over a darker foreground; automatist: middle (judgement)
surrealism.composition: illusionistic: deep empty stage, low horizon, few isolated objects; automatist: all-over field with floating biomorphic signs (judgement)
surrealism.drawing: illusionistic: precise graphite drawing, convincing modelling of impossible juxtapositions, double images; automatist: fast unplanned line, then read and defined (Philadelphia, Tate, Pompidou)
surrealism.edges: illusionistic: soft within forms, crisp at silhouettes; automatist: lost field edges, crisp lines

marks.length: illusionistic: short hidden; automatist: long continuous lines
marks.direction: illusionistic follows form; automatist free

process: illusionistic: find the juxtaposition or double image; precise drawing on a smooth light ground; thin lay-in; soft modelling and sharp cast shadows; highest finish on the strange object
automatist: lay a stained or textured field; automatic drawing at speed; look and read the forms; define a few, leave the field open
finishing: illusionistic: low-opacity unifying glaze, then varnish when available
automatist: stop when forms are found and the field breathes; no glaze (judgement)
pitfalls: pastiche: melting clocks, bowler hats, floating apples, ants, crutches
fantasy-illustration kitsch and random weirdness without one charged relation
automatist mode as pretty doodle
nearest wrong feelings: whimsy, explicit horror, cold cleverness
engine_gaps: no chance-texture tools (frottage, decalcomania, grattage over a textured object)
no varnish step for oil
no mixed media or sand
no way to suppress planning for automatic drawing
ink medium needed for automatic drawing
sources: Tate, Frottage / Grattage / Decalcomania / Biomorphic / Automatism art terms
Philadelphia Museum of Art, Dalí teacher resource: https://legacyweb.philamuseum.org/doc_downloads/education/ex_resources/dali.pdf
Fundació Gala-Salvador Dalí, Painting and Documenting the painting technique

layer_order.source: docs/styles/surrealism.md section 9 (illusionistic): precise drawing on a smooth light ground; thin lay-in; soft modelling and sharp cast shadows; highest finish on the strange object.
layer_order.judgement: the automatist mode lays its field before the drawing; this order is the illusionistic one.

abstract-expressionism.name: Abstract Expressionism (gestural and colour field)
technique: gestural: sweeping large-brush marks, poured/trailed/flicked paint, wet-into-wet layering, building up and scraping down
colour field: tinted size stain, thin wet-on-wet field layers, feathered edges, egg and dammar glazes

palette.principle: gestural: reduced (black/raw canvas) or all-over interlace, colour as energy (judgement); colour field: two or three colours in thin luminous layers (Tate Papers 23 pigments)

abstract-expressionism.light: no depicted light; gestural energy from value contrast; colour field light from within thin stacked layers and soft edges (judgement)
abstract-expressionism.value_key: gestural: mixed, often high contrast; colour field: low and close-valued or saturated mid (judgement)
abstract-expressionism.composition: gestural: all-over or a few big strokes in tension; colour field: frontal, vertical, soft rectangles or bands in a field; big, enveloping scale (Met)
abstract-expressionism.drawing: gestural: drawing in paint at full arm, figures emerging and dissolving; colour field: the soft rectangle or band as the only form
abstract-expressionism.edges: gestural: varied, broken, dragged; colour field: feathered, soft (Tate Papers 23)

marks.direction: free, from the body's gesture

process: gestural: raw canvas; unplanned first marks, thin; wet-into-wet layers in quick succession; look and respond, build up and scrape down; stop when the event holds together

colour field: tinted glue size stained into raw canvas; thin field layers wet on wet a day apart; dammar sealing glaze; feathered under-colour at figure edges; figure colour last; egg and dammar glazes
finishing: gestural: no varnish or unifying glaze; judge the event complete
colour field: very low-opacity glazes over parts of the field only, unevenly
pitfalls: pastiche: drip-splatter or two rectangles on maroon
random noise without a felt arc
digital gradients
nearest wrong feelings: default chaos/anger in gestural, decor or wellness calm in colour field
engine_gaps: no pour/drip tool
no flick or splatter
no floor orientation or gravity flow
no raw-canvas absorption or soak-stain
no matte/gloss render variation
no subtractive scrape
no newspaper transfer
no enamel/house-paint behaviour
sources: Tate Papers 23, Conserving Rothko's Black on Maroon: https://www.tate.org.uk/research/tate-papers/23/conserving-mark-rothkos-black-on-maroon-1958-the-construction-of-a-representative-sample-and-the-removal-of-graffiti-ink
Tate, Women Singing II, Process and Memory: https://www.tate.org.uk/research/in-focus/women-singing-ii/process-and-memory

layer_order.source: docs/styles/abstract-expressionism.md section 9: unplanned thin first marks (gestural) or a stained field (colour field); wet-into-wet layers or thin field layers; the figure colour and final glazes last.
layer_order.judgement: both modes collapsed into first marks, building layers, last marks; building up and scraping down are corrections and not ordered.

ukiyo-e.name: Ukiyo-e (woodblock prints and painted ukiyo-e)
ukiyo-e.period: Japan, Edo period (1615-1868); full-colour nishiki-e from 1765
technique: sumi key line enclosing flat water-based colour areas
one colour per block, printed in sequence with registration
blind embossing and mica as luxury finishes

palette.principle: limited flat water-based colours, about ten or more impressions; indigo/dayflower blues then Prussian blue (Vermeulen et al. 2020); hexes approximate aged prints (judgement)

ukiyo-e.light: no modelled light or cast shadows; time and weather carried by flat colour fields and bokashi (AAM, Fitzwilliam)
ukiyo-e.value_key: high to middle; paper is the lightest value (judgement)
ukiyo-e.composition: strong diagonals, high or low viewpoints, cropped foreground at the frame, asymmetry, graded sky bands; narrow formats force vertical crops (judgement; formats from Fitzwilliam)
ukiyo-e.drawing: clean closed key line carries form; typified elongated figures; textiles as flat pattern (AAM; judgement on character)

marks.direction: lines follow contour; fills invisible

process: line design as a schema of key lines and colour zones
flat colour areas one colour at a time, lightest first, clipped to zones, paper left showing
bokashi bands and pattern
key line in sumi over the colour (brushed analogue; historically key block first)
line corrections; embossing/mica when available; sign
finishing: no varnish
optional blind embossing or mica as finish ops when the medium supports them
stop at clean flat areas; no added shading (judgement)
pitfalls: orientalist postcard: Great Wave, Fuji, cherry blossom, geisha, torii
pastiche of a named design; fake seals or Japanese signatures
vector clip-art flatness
bokashi everywhere as airbrush
nearest wrong feelings: decorative prettiness, tourist exoticism, anime-cute faces
engine_gaps: woodblock-print look medium not yet available (gouache on paper as proxy)
no paper fibre texture
no embossing or mica render
no registration-offset model
no one-colour-per-block constraint
no zone-fill planning helper
sources: Met, Woodblock Prints in the Ukiyo-e Style: https://www.metmuseum.org/en/essays/woodblock-prints-in-the-ukiyo-e-style
Asian Art Museum, The ukiyo-e woodblock printing process: https://education.asianart.org/resources/the-ukiyo-e-woodblock-printing-process/
Vermeulen et al. 2020, npj Heritage Science 8:62, doi:10.1186/s40494-020-00406-y

layer_order.source: docs/styles/ukiyo-e.md section 9 and styles.json process: the line design; flat colour areas lightest first and bokashi; the key line in sumi over the colour (the brushed analogue).
layer_order.judgement: historically the key block was cut first; the studio's brushed analogue lays it last, as styles.json says.

east-asian-ink.name: East Asian ink painting (literati landscape and sumi-e)
east-asian-ink.period: China from the Tang (landscape) and Song/Yuan (literati); Japan, late Kamakura and Muromachi (suibokuga) onward
technique: outline then texture strokes (cun) then graded washes then dots
blank paper for water, mist and snow

palette.principle: ink is the colour: one black in many dilutions; light blue-green and red-orange/ochre washes secondary (AAM Brushstrokes). Hex tones are judgement.
avoid: mineral blue-green court style unless chosen

east-asian-ink.light: no consistent light source; light and dark from ink tone and bare paper; mist bands separate planes (Cahill; AAM)
east-asian-ink.value_key: high: mostly paper and pale wash, darkest ink in few accents (judgement)
east-asian-ink.composition: mountain and water; main mountain with subordinates; three distances (high, deep, level); stacked near-middle-far with mist; paths, small figures and pavilions to enter; large blanks; inscription/seal placed in an active area (AAM; Cahill)
east-asian-ink.drawing: line first ('making boundaries'); cun texture strokes by rock type with set brush angles; dots for foliage and moss; boneless leaves; form by type from stored observation, not a model (AAM; Guo Xi via Cahill)
east-asian-ink.edges: crisp on sized paper, soft and fuzzy bleeding on unsized paper; flying-white broken edges

marks.length: from dots to long continuous lines
marks.direction: follows the structure of rock, tree and water; calligraphic

process: grind ink to the needed tones; choose brush and paper
observe, then paint from the image held in the mind
literati: main forms in pale-to-middle outline, near to far
cun texture strokes
graded washes with water, blanks left
dots and darkest accents last
inscription and seal (Teodor: signature)
xieyi: pale tones, then darker into the still-wet ink, then accents and flying-white lines
finishing: stop while fresh: vitality over completeness
last dots and dark accents
sign in an active area that balances the composition, as a seal would be placed
no fake seals or invented characters
pitfalls: orientalist postcard: panda, red sun, crane and moon, pagoda, straw-hat fisherman, tourist karsts
Zen decor minimalism
fake calligraphy and seals
Western single light source, perspective, full coverage, overpainting
grey mush without dark accents or white
nearest wrong feelings: generic spa calm, default melancholy
engine_gaps: ink medium and paper absorption not yet available
no brush-angle parameter (upright vs slanted tip)
no multi-tone loading in one brush
no permanence rule forbidding covering
transfer should be optional and faint
sources: Met, Landscape Painting in Chinese Art: https://www.metmuseum.org/TOAH/HD/clpg/hd_clpg.htm
Asian Art Museum, Brushstrokes: Styles and Techniques of Chinese Painting: https://education.asianart.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2019/09/Brushstrokes.pdf
Cleveland Museum of Art, Haboku Landscape: https://www.clevelandart.org/art/148810
Xie He Six Principles: ibiblio Cultural Heritage of China; HKU University Museum, Huihua Liufa

layer_order.source: docs/styles/east-asian-ink.md section 9: main forms in pale-to-middle outline; cun texture strokes; graded washes; dots and darkest accents last.
layer_order.judgement: the outline mapped to drawing (it is the structure, painted once) and the cun strokes to body; the order of dots is the doc's own judgement.

realism.name: Realism
technique: lights built thick out of the dark

palette.principle: restricted earth-dominated tonal palette organised by value; subdued local colour, few strong accents (judgement)

realism.light: contrast of light and dark guides the eye; lights opaque and loaded, shadows thin and warm, close to the ground
realism.composition: ordinary subjects at monumental scale; frieze rows or one labourer filling the frame; rocks, earth and water close to the viewer; depth by overlap, little atmospheric perspective
realism.drawing: solid generalised masses with weight and posture; academic scale and perspective may be broken; space can flatten
realism.edges: firm where mass meets mass, lost into the dark ground in shadow

marks.direction: follows the material: troweled rock, dragged earth, laid water

process: studies from observation (schema/blockout)
dark warm ground over the canvas
thin lay-in of the big masses in dark-middle values, ground left as shadow
build the lights with loaded brush and knife, handling each material in its own way; revise freely
last lightest knife accents and darkest accents
charcoal: block-in, stumped masses, darks reinforced, lights lifted, contour accents, fixative
finishing: resolved weighty image, not a polished academic surface
lightest knife accents and darkest accents last
optional very light warm unifying glaze in place of a natural-resin varnish (judgement)
charcoal: fixative over the finished sheet; signed in the medium lower right
pitfalls: brown-gravy museum filter with no value structure
sentimental genre picture (pity instead of gravity)
photographic hyper-realism
Teodor's own hushed bittersweet dark-room habit
heroic propaganda or academic polish
engine_gaps: charcoal medium not built yet (stick vs compressed, stumping, paper tooth)
no subtractive tool for lifting or scraping
no varnish or fixative finishing step
single-constant KM makes earth darks slightly chalky

layer_order.source: docs/styles/realism.md section 9: studies; thin lay-in of the big masses in dark-middle values over a dark ground; lights built with loaded brush and knife; last lightest knife accents and darkest accents.
layer_order.judgement: the lay-in is in colour but tonal, so underpainting and dead_colour are one stage.

impressionism.name: Impressionism
technique: open network of strokes with ground showing

palette.principle: pure, mostly unmixed spectral colours plus white; shadows and highlights in colour; no black

impressionism.light: specific outdoor light (hour, season, weather); modelling by colour temperature; shadows blue/violet/green
impressionism.composition: modern leisure and urban life, planned under spontaneous handling; horizon set early, whole canvas worked together; casual cropping (judgement)
impressionism.drawing: no underdrawing; thin lay-in in subdued colour; strokes barely convey forms; figures as a few gestural strokes
impressionism.edges: soft and broken everywhere; hard only for rare accents

marks.direction: follows form or the light, varied

process: off-white ground
thin lay-in of main elements in subdued colour, horizon set early
build the whole together, moving between areas, surroundings brought up around forms
wet-in-wet upper layers, figures painted into wet surroundings; some strokes over dry
reinforce: intense local colour on top, reflections last, thin dragged strokes, corners reinforced
pastel: linear and stumped layers, fixative only as a barrier in selected areas
finishing: no varnish, no unifying glaze
last accents and reflections; ground may show
finished when the light effect is complete, not when the surface is closed (judgement)
pastel: no overall fixative (it darkens and dulls)
pitfalls: chocolate-box pastiche (lilies, parasols, sweet pinks, uniform commas)
over-blending into mush
grey-black shadows
sweet nostalgia or generic pleasantness instead of a specific moment
do_match strokes too uniform and too obedient to the schema
engine_gaps: pastel medium not built yet (toned paper tooth, stick skipping, stumping, selective fixative)
no light model for hour and weather (the schema must carry it)
no deliberate complementary placement per stroke, only colour jitter

layer_order.source: docs/styles/impressionism.md section 9: thin lay-in of the main elements in subdued colour; the whole built together wet-in-wet; reinforce and accent: intense local colour on top, reflections last, thin dragged strokes late.
layer_order.judgement: the late thin dragged strokes (scumbles) can also come with the accents; scumble is placed with the body stage.

fauvism.name: Fauvism
technique: colour almost straight from the tube

palette.principle: saturated hues juxtaposed in complementary pairs; colour contrast instead of shadow; white ground as the lightest light

fauvism.light: intense and everywhere; hardly any shadows; volume and depth by colour contrast; thickest paint where light is strongest
fauvism.composition: flat pictorial space of colour zones, each with its own stroke direction and density; key line (horizon) set first; no traditional perspective
fauvism.drawing: forms simplified toward abstraction; layout in a thin blue line or light ultramarine; no compositional changes
fauvism.edges: hard by juxtaposition; thin dark fluid contour lines where shapes would merge

marks.direction: per zone: radiating from the light, horizontal for water
marks.spacing: strokes rarely overlapping, a distance apart

process: drawing from the motif close in form and colour
bright white ground intended to stay visible (or no ground, thick single layers)
layout with thin blue line or light ultramarine glazes
key line first, then zones with their own stroke direction
direct, mostly wet-in-wet patches of nearly pure colour; few layers, no reworking
thin dark contour lines where shapes would merge (order is judgement)
finishing: no varnish tone (yellowed varnishes on Fauve pictures were non-original and removed)
stop while the ground still breathes (judgement)
no glazes, no blending, no last darks except contours
pitfalls: random 'wild colour' filter over a naturalistic picture
filling every gap and covering the white ground
complementaries greyed by high wetmix
decorative holiday-poster prettiness
drifting into Expressionist anguish or Teodor's hushed dark interior
engine_gaps: no stroke-spacing control (only count)
no zone-wise complementary palette rule
do_match closes the surface; use free strokes or low cover
unprimed canvas absorbency not modelled

layer_order.source: docs/styles/fauvism.md section 9: layout in a thin blue line or light ultramarine glazes; key line first, then zones of nearly pure colour painted directly; thin dark contour lines where shapes would merge.
layer_order.judgement: direct painting has no separate dead colour, so the first colour and the body are one stage; the doc marks the contours' order as judgement.

expressionism.name: German Expressionism (Brücke)

media_notes.ink: the woodcut look: flat black relief on paper; no relief-print medium exists yet

technique: thin lean matte colour (little binder, wax in benzine)
woodcut: gouged whites, black relief, wood grain

palette.principle: vivid non-naturalistic high-chroma colour for tension and contrast; aniline colours; matte not glossy; black for contour and woodcut

expressionism.light: no consistent source; high value and colour contrast; flickering lights without sources; woodcut two values only
expressionism.composition: crowded city streets with compressed space, or nudes in nature; rhythm of figures by repeated marks; woodcut compositions reversed
expressionism.drawing: simplified, distorted, angular forms; underdrawn and planned, but forms change during work
expressionism.edges: hard, angular, splintered contours; hatching edges

marks.direction: hatched diagonals and sharp rays; angular

process: seeds: sketchbook impressions, charcoal, pastel colour trials, prints of the motif
underdrawing on canvas
thin lean vivid colour fields, drying matte
rework and restate; forms change in the process
hatching and dark contours last (judgement)
charcoal: broad strokes, hatched contours, wash or stumping, emphasis lines, fixative
woodcut look: flat black masses, then hard white cuts painted over (Teodor proxy)
finishing: no varnish: the Brücke painters avoided gloss
no glaze; matte surface
process energy left visible within a planned image
woodcut: grain and uneven inking accepted; charcoal: fixative
pitfalls: horror-poster pastiche (green faces, screaming masks as a filter)
glossy thick oil impasto
random scribble instead of planned energy
Fauvist joy, generic angst, or Teodor's hushed bittersweet habit
engine_gaps: no woodcut / relief-print medium; no subtractive cut; no wood-grain texture
charcoal medium not built yet
no matte surface parameter (render adds specular on height)
Der Blaue Reiter needs its own entry

layer_order.source: docs/styles/expressionism.md section 9: underdrawing; thin lean colour fields; rework and restate; hatching and dark contours last.
layer_order.judgement: the doc marks the order of hatching and contours as judgement.

pen-and-ink-illustration.name: Pen-and-ink illustration (drawing for process reproduction)
pen-and-ink-illustration.period: Europe and the United States, c. 1880-1920 (book and magazine illustration for photomechanical line blocks)
technique: outline as the main convention, broken in the light
parallel hatching for tone, cross-hatching only for deep quiet shadows
several nibs in one drawing (fine for distance, broad for foreground)
few and positive values; work kept open for reduction
lots of white paper (economy of means)
corrections by scraping, never patched lines

palette.principle: one black India ink on white board; tone only from line density (a line block prints black or nothing: Harper 1894). Board colour measured on the references as they look today; fresh board is whiter (judgement).
avoid: closely knit grey tones that close up in reduction

pen-and-ink-illustration.light: one clear light; shadows hatched; most of the sheet is paper (measured: lights 0.82 ± 0.15, key L* 77 ± 8, n = 58)
pen-and-ink-illustration.value_key: high: brilliant blacks and large light areas, just enough half-tone (Maginnis 1898)
pen-and-ink-illustration.composition: vignettes and full-page plates; white areas carry the light; a foreground black accent; story and figures first, backgrounds suggested (judgement; Maginnis on colour-schemes)
pen-and-ink-illustration.drawing: outline first and most important; texture by line character; lines clear and distinct; sharp-angle cross-hatch (measured crossing angle 62°, 50-70)
pen-and-ink-illustration.edges: all hard: pen lines, no soft edges; light eats into broken outlines

marks.length: short hatching flicks to long contours
marks.direction: hatching by plane, contours following the form

process: pencil study on Bristol board (pencil tool or transfer)
outline and principal darks in pen, several nibs
tones by hatching, light to dark, few positive values, work kept open
deepest shadows cross-hatched at a sharp angle
scrape corrections; erase pencil
check at reduced size (look thumb), sign
finishing: finish erase-pencil
last blacks
finish scrape for a lost light
check the drawing reduced (the diminishing glass)
stop: finished means printable, not polished
pitfalls: grey mush: tones too dense or too close
mechanical machine-ruled hatching everywhere
pastiche of a famous illustrator's look (Art Nouveau black masses, costume romance)
nearest wrong feelings: quaint nostalgia, greeting-card charm, colouring-book outline
engine_gaps: core hatch does not follow the form or vary spacing within one intention
no reduced-size print preview
no Chinese white (opaque correction)
no clay-board or scratchboard
sources: C. D. Maginnis, Pen Drawing: An Illustrated Treatise (1898): https://archive.org/details/pendrawingillust00magi ; https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/17502
C. G. Harper, A Practical Hand-book of Drawing for Modern Methods of Reproduction (1894): https://archive.org/stream/apracticalhandb00harpgoog/apracticalhandb00harpgoog_djvu.txt

layer_order.source: docs/styles/pen-and-ink-illustration.md section 9: pencil study; outline and principal darks in pen; tones by hatching light to dark, a second closer hatching and cross-hatching only in the deepest shadow; last blacks and pen edge accents.
layer_order.judgement: the pen outline on bare board is mapped to drawing with the pencil study (the studio infers drawing for a pen on bare ground); the second hatching and the cross-hatching are the same hatch stage; the last blacks and edge accents over the hatching share the last stage (the studio infers contour or accent from their darkness); scraping, Chinese white and erasing the pencil are corrections and not ordered.

etching-engraving.name: Etching and engraving (intaglio printmaking)
etching-engraving.period: Europe, burin engraving c. 1470-1700 (reproductive engraving to the 19th century), etching from the 16th century, the etching revival c. 1850-1900
technique: burin engraving: swelling and tapering lines in systems of parallel and cross-hatching, dots in the lozenges
etching: an even, free needle line bitten in stages with stopping-out (deeper = wider and darker)
printing: wiped plate, plate tone, retroussage, platemark

palette.principle: one printing ink, black or warm brown, on cream laid or wove paper; tone = lines + bite + plate tone. Ink absorption measured on the references; paper measured as photographed today.
avoid: wash tones without lines (aquatint and mezzotint are other techniques)

etching-engraving.light: engraving: consistent light, hatching swelling into shadow and crossing in the deepest darks; etching: value from density, needle size and bite (Lalanne)
etching-engraving.value_key: middle-light (measured: key L* 67 ± 10, spread 18.5 ± 3.8, darks 0.09 ± 0.09, n = 60)
etching-engraving.composition: the plate rectangle and platemark frame the image with a paper margin; engraving fills the plate; etching vignettes toward the edges and leaves skies as paper (judgement); no lettering or fake inscriptions
etching-engraving.drawing: engraving: form by systems of curved parallels, crossing at ~55° (measured), dots and flecks; etching: free, even line, open outline, finer needles and shorter bites for distance
etching-engraving.edges: hard, fine lines; drypoint burr soft on one side; plate tone softens the ground between lines

marks.length: long steady lines (burin); free lines of any length (needle)
marks.direction: systems following the form (engraving); free hatching in several directions (etching)

process: engraving: outlines with the burin, hatching systems light to dark, dots in the lozenges, clean wipe
etching: needle drawing bitten 3-4 min, stop out the lights, bite again (6, then 8 min more in the darks), drypoint accents
platemark, wipe (plate tone, retroussage), sign
finishing: finish platemark
finish wipe (engraving clean: tone 0.02; etching: tone 0.04-0.06, retroussage 0.2-0.4)
a few drypoint accents
sign
pitfalls: digital line-art look: even lines with no swell, bite or plate tone
over-biting into black mud
pastiche of famous plates
nearest wrong feelings: antiquarian quaintness, banknote stiffness, the souvenir view
engine_gaps: core hatch is a draughtsman's (±15% spacing, short pieces): an engraver's regular systems and form-following curves need strokes or a regular hatch
no aquatint, mezzotint or soft-ground
no reversal of the image by the press
plate tone and platemark depth by eye
sources: Met, The Printed Image in the West: Engraving / Etching / Drypoint (W. Thompson 2003): https://www.metmuseum.org/en/essays/the-printed-image-in-the-west-engraving
Met, Materials and Techniques: Printmaking: Engraving / Etching: https://www.metmuseum.org/en/perspectives/materials-and-techniques-printmaking-etching
M. Lalanne, A Treatise on Etching, trans. Koehler (1880): https://archive.org/details/treatiseonetchin00lalauoft
G. J. Brown, Dotted Lozenge: Goltzius, Prints and Principles (2012): https://www.printsandprinciples.com/2012/11/goltzius-dotted-lozenge.html
Princeton Graphic Arts, Laid or Wove: https://www.princeton.edu/~graphicarts/2008/03/laid_or_wove.html
The Met Open Access (CC0): studio/targets.parts/etching-engraving.json, studio/calibration_refs.parts/etching-engraving.json, MetObjects.csv record counts

layer_order.source: docs/styles/etching-engraving.md section 9: outlines with the burin or needle; systems of hatching light to dark; dots and flicks (engraving) or drypoint accents (etching) last.
layer_order.judgement: the biting stages, platemark and wiping are finishing operations on lines already laid, not layers, and are not ordered; the burin's or needle's accents over the hatching share the last stage (the studio infers contour or accent from their darkness); burnishing and scraping are corrections and not ordered.

graphite-hyperrealism.name: Graphite hyperrealism
graphite-hyperrealism.period: USA and Europe, from photorealism (late 1960s) and hyperrealism (1970s on); graphite practice continuing today
technique: transfer by grid, projection or tracing
indented white lines before any tone
layered tone, hard over soft, many light passes in crossed directions
lifting lights with kneaded, pen and battery erasers
carbon pencil or powder past graphite's darkest

palette.principle: monochrome: the paper's white to graphite's dark grey, carbon for the darkest darks; the photograph's full value range as far as the media allow
avoid: glare of over-burnished soft graphite in the darks

graphite-hyperrealism.light: one photographic light; soft penumbras and dark contact shadows as the camera records them
graphite-hyperrealism.value_key: full (photographic): key about L* 50, spread about 21, p5-p95 L* 17-82 (measured on public-domain photographs)
graphite-hyperrealism.composition: the photograph's: close crops, objects or faces filling the frame, shallow depth of field, lens perspective; studio tests such as an egg under one light or crumpled paper
graphite-hyperrealism.drawing: transferred from the photograph mechanically or semi-mechanically, then built as tone; no contour lines survive
graphite-hyperrealism.edges: crisp in the focal plane, lost and soft out of focus (depth of field); hard-edge share near a photograph's (about 0.17)

marks.length: short, layered, crossed; invisible at viewing distance
marks.direction: crossed in several directions, then blended

process: photograph (schema)
transfer the outline lightly (grid, projection or tracing)
indent the white lines
tone in value bands, darkest first, hard over soft
blend each part in stages, masked at the edges
correct against the photograph: layer, blend, repeat
lift the lights
darkest accents, clean margins, optional fixative
finishing: finished when it looks like the photograph: no visible strokes at viewing distance, smooth gradients, full value range, photographic edges
highlights lifted last; darkest accents in carbon or the softest graphite
fixative optional (dulls shine, can darken)
pitfalls: overblended airbrushed plastic look
graphite glare in forced darks
outline or hatching left showing
technical demonstration with no subject; clinical coldness
engine_gaps: value bands step at their edges (core hatch has no feathering at a layer boundary)
match corrections leave dashes that need blending
per-part masks are written by hand as polygons
graphite and carbon cannot reach a photograph's blacks (by nature)
fixed raking light for the sheen
2400x3200 works but takes about an hour for a full drawing on 2 vCPU
judgement_calls: default support vellum among the three the sources name
palette greys (from the engine's grade values)

layer_order.source: docs/styles/graphite-hyperrealism.md process: mechanical transfer of the outline (drawing); tone built in layers from soft to hard grades over the whole passage (body); blending passes with brush, tortillon and chamois that unify each layer (glaze: a unifying film); lights lifted with erasers and last darks and edges (correction, accent).
layer_order.judgement: blending passes are mapped to glaze as the unifying layer, since the engine has no blend role; indents are made before shading but are not a role. Hatch is accepted as body for graphite.
